summary: Created at the user's request during MPI-441 close-out. The pre-commit hook prints "flip to strict mode in a separate tracker once clean" and no such tracker existed. 19 warnings across 9 files; the 4 require-destroy-on-events hits are real teardown leaks, the rest mechanical.

todo -> doing. Re-measured 2026-08-08: 20 warnings / 0 errors. Drift from the card: MpiAppLibrary.js was renamed MpiFlowLibrary.js, and heroStats.js carries 5 require-destroy-on-events hits, not 4. The 2 null-ruleId messages are unused eslint-disable directives at footprint.js:203 and :206 (reportUnusedDisableDirectives) - stale comments to delete, not violations to fix.

maturity -> validating. Lint is strict and green: eslint js/ --max-warnings=0 exits 0, npm test 508/508. TWO card errors corrected. (1) 'Drop --max-warnings=9999' is NOT the flip - eslint's default is unlimited, so dropping the flag leaves the gate wide open (measured: 20 warnings, exit 0). All three sites are now --max-warnings=0. (2) The hook's real gate was 'npx lint-staged || true', which swallows every failure regardless of the flag; the card never mentioned it. Hook is now the single line 'npx lint-staged'. Acceptance 2 is the one open question for the user: the 5 require-destroy-on-events hits are NOT leaks. initHeroStats runs exactly once (init.js -> initShell -> initHeroStats) and its subscriptions are app-lifetime by design, the same category as ~25 sites in shell.js that all carry 'eslint-disable-next-line mpi/require-destroy-on-events -- app-lifetime listener'. I applied that documented convention rather than inventing a destroyHeroStats() nobody calls. Also fixed for real: js/pages/components.js used --text-primary/--text-secondary, which DO NOT EXIST (each used once, nowhere defined), so the #fff/#aaa fallbacks were what rendered - now --ink-1/--ink-2. The 2 null-ruleId messages were unused no-console disable directives (no-console is not configured at all) - deleted.
